verdicts.reasoning: Both teams reached the same, correct root cause (no owner of the vocabulary; cross-vocabulary string comparisons silently False) and chose the same architecture: str enums, explicit total mappings, one cue matcher, one domain resolver, one health classifier, a BOM table, an AST literal-ban test and an in-repo TS generator. Checked in code: readiness._STAGE_SCORE knows launched/scaling only (readiness.py:22), frontend journeyStore spells registered_with_product while models/enums.py has registered_product, and core/ has no vocab module. B is wiser on three points that matter for correctness. (1) B noticed that Python's \b splits Tamil words at combining vowel signs; I verified re.findall(r'\b\w+\b') returns 6 tokens for a two-word Tamil phrase, so A's plain \b cue regexes would produce exactly the inside-a-word false hits the theme is about once Tamil text reaches the matcher. (2) B's primary-sector rule prefers the founder's explicit answer and lowers confidence on a tie so the engine confirms, where A takes first position in text, which can silently pick the wrong primary. (3) B's rollout keeps a shrinking allowlist so the ban test can be blocking without a big-bang change, adds a Hypothesis property test for the matcher and asks the owner to sign off on the judgement-laden mapping tables. A is wiser on one point: it makes the stored-session upgrade explicit (vocab.upgrade_slot_value called from AgentSession.from_dict) instead of relying on B's reference to a separate 2.1.4 upgrade step that may not exist yet. A's single-file module is slightly simpler, but B's package split is reasonable for ~9 concerns. B's Language enum is scope for T26 and is kept only as a small file since it costs nothing. Final: B's design and plan, with A's explicit from_dict upgrade path and A's 'interfaces' clarity about T03/T04/T05/T06 usage.

final.chosen: Canonical vocabulary package app/core/vocab (str Enums + explicit total mapping tables + one Tamil-safe cue matcher + one domain resolver + one health classifier + BOM table), an AST literal-ban test with a shrinking allowlist, an explicit stored-session upgrade in AgentSession.from_dict, and a generated TypeScript vocabulary file checked in CI.
final.why_chosen: It removes the root cause (no owner of meaning) instead of patching boundaries; it is deterministic, offline and dependency-free (decision 0002); it reuses slots.Sector, taxonomy.py's compiled cues/NIC tables and registry.detect_domain. The Tamil-safe boundary (from B) prevents cue false hits on Tamil text, which plain \b does not; the founder-first primary-sector rule with confirmation on ties avoids silent wrong picks; the explicit from_dict upgrade (from A) guarantees old sessions load without depending on another task. Gives T03, T04, T05, T06, T21, T26 and T31 the types they need.

approaches.name: Canonical vocabulary module/package (StrEnums + explicit mapping tables + one cue matcher + AST literal-ban test + generated TS)
approaches.advantages: One meaning per value; mismatches become import, validation or test errors; one matcher fixes substring false hits everywhere; frontend cannot drift; zero dependencies; offline.
approaches.drawbacks: Wide migration touching about ten backend modules and four frontend pages; stored sessions need an alias upgrade; mapping tables embed judgement needing owner sign-off.

approaches.name: Boundary normalisers / per-module alias tables
approaches.advantages: Small, independent diffs; fast.
approaches.drawbacks: Internal literals (K_DOMAIN, _scheme_rules, idea_type, readiness) keep drifting; every new consumer must remember to normalise; nothing fails when it forgets; no single coverage test.

approaches.name: Shared YAML/JSON vocabulary data file loaded by Python and TypeScript
approaches.advantages: One language-neutral file; editable by non-coders.
approaches.drawbacks: Second schema system beside Pydantic; use sites revert to strings without static checking; mapping logic still lives in Python; extra runtime asset for the frontend.

approaches.name: OpenAPI-generated TypeScript types (openapi-typescript)
approaches.advantages: Covers every request/response type, not only vocabularies.
approaches.drawbacks: Fixes only the browser edge, not the in-process Python mismatches that cause most symptoms; adds an npm devDependency and an export step.

approaches.name: Learned or fuzzy classification (rapidfuzz, scikit-learn, free model) into the vocabulary
approaches.advantages: Tolerates unseen wording.
approaches.drawbacks: Silent wrong matches on short words, no labelled data, not explainable, needs network on a model path, contradicts decision 0002.

not_chosen.name: Boundary normalisers / per-module alias tables
not_chosen.reason: Patches symptoms and leaves several vocabularies; the next consumer or new word repeats the bug and nothing can test coverage.

not_chosen.name: Shared YAML/JSON vocabulary data file
not_chosen.reason: Loses static typing at use sites and duplicates Pydantic; the curated tables are just as reviewable as Python next to the enums.

not_chosen.name: OpenAPI-generated TypeScript types
not_chosen.reason: Only the browser edge; the ~40-line in-repo exporter covers these enums now without an npm dependency. Revisit under 5.3.4.

not_chosen.name: Learned or fuzzy classification
not_chosen.reason: Reproduces the silent wrong-match bug being fixed, has no labelled data, is not explainable and contradicts decision 0002 (code decides from reviewed tables).

verdicts.reasoning: Both teams found the same cause (no per-item provenance with one validator and one freshness rule; harvest scripts write instead of merge) and chose the same solution: a Pydantic Provenance block, one freshness helper with per-dataset max ages, strict registry loader, draft/not-covered/translation honesty, merge-based harvest, and a reusable data-checks workflow plus create-pull-request on a fixed branch and a freshness issue instead of a clock gate. B is a little stronger: it gives every data file a typed Pydantic model (DomainCard, RegulatoryItem, PackPrice, Scheme, IntakeRecord, InvestorSignal, DomainSignal, Translation) validated at load and in one test, so A's separate check_data.py script is not needed; it re-fetches signals when the trend query changes (trend_query_hash), not only by age; it records consecutive_failures; it explored the PAT/GitHub App option and rejected it for a sound reason (long-lived secret); it adds actionlint; and it anchors claims to file:line (registry.py:52/:64/:191-192, phrasebook.py:50-52, weekly-checks.yml:38-55). B also maps F-A5-014 to both the per-scheme date and the freshness issue, which is the complete fix. A contributes atomic writes in the harvest scripts (temp file then replace, so a crash mid-write cannot truncate a data file) and an explicit ok-count guard threshold (fail the step if ok-records drop by more than half), which B only names as 'shrink guard'. A's 'date not recorded' wording for null checked_on is folded into B's never_checked label. Final: B's design and plan with A's atomic writes and explicit shrink threshold.

final.chosen: Per-item Provenance block on typed Pydantic dataset models + one freshness helper with per-dataset max ages + merge-based, atomic, incremental harvest scripts + GitHub Actions hardening (reusable data-checks workflow, isolated steps, one rolling PR via create-pull-request, freshness issue instead of a clock gate).
final.why_chosen: The thirteen flags reduce to two missing things: item-level provenance with one validator, and a harvest pipeline that merges and isolates failures. Pydantic is already the stack's validator so the same models validate at load and in CI with no new dependency; the freshness helper turns 'last checked on' into one function used by intake, investors, schemes and the weekly report. Data stays in git for review and works offline. Workflow changes use built-in workflow_call and one SHA-pinned action, with no secret to rotate.

design.data_model: Every curated item gains provenance with honest values, never invented dates: cards keep review; regulatory items and pack prices get checked_on null with their existing source or null; funding-catalogue entries get checked_on null unless the owner confirms. Harvest records gain last_attempt and consecutive_failures. signals.json domains gain checked_on and trend_query_hash. translations.json keeps reviewed.
design.algorithm: Freshness: stale if today - checked_on > MAX_AGE_DAYS[dataset]; never_checked if null. Draft wording: _domain_row/_roadmap carry review; offline template and grounding add 'from a draft card, not yet checked by a reviewer'; the model gets review in the tool result plus a system rule. Uncovered district: 'I do not have district data for Salem yet, so I cannot say how well this fits there' plus a structlog counter district.not_covered (district only, no person). translation(text, lang): None unless reviewed or setting on; callers fall back to English. Investor reachability: stale signals -> status 'stale', score as 'not checked', labelled. Incremental signals: domains missing, older than 180 days or with changed trend_query_hash, oldest first, --max per run (default 60); on BudgetExhausted write completed domains and exit 0 with a summary.

verdicts.reasoning: Both teams correctly located the cause at ElicitationSession.put (session.py:153-171: Any value, confidence-only precedence, no outcome) and both fix it there with a codec over answers.validate, a source rank table, rivals and a PutOutcome, plus a bounded ProfileIn and client/server profile projections. The difference is the precedence policy, and there A is right and B has two correctness problems. (1) B ranks CHOSEN (6) above ANSWER (5), and its algorithm keeps a higher-rank value against any lower-rank write, so once a founder picks a lever or card their later spoken correction is silently kept_existing: the founder can no longer change their own mind. A ranks CHOSEN equal to ANSWER and lets a later direct answer to that slot's question (answering=True) or an explicit correction replace it, which is what F-B1-016 needs. (2) For F-B4-012 the flag's own resolution (tree-p1.md:208) says neither guess is trusted blindly: a disagreement caps confidence below the ask threshold so the founder is asked. B makes NOTE outrank EXTRACTED, so the model's note simply replaces the extractor's guess with no question; A treats both as equal low rank and turns the disagreement into a conflict that the selector asks, matching the resolution. On thresholds (F-A1-009), A defines KNOWN/ASSUMED/UNKNOWN bands that keep today's 0.5 'filled' floor and feed T05's 'I assumed' restatement, while B raises filled to 0.60 and admits it may add questions. A also returns profile_ignored so the screen can say what will be asked. B contributes good details: the codec as its own small module, a Hypothesis property test (stored value is absent or of the declared type; build_plan never raises), healing stored sessions through a model_validator on ElicitationSession (which is a Pydantic BaseModel, session.py:82), the rule that profile values reached only by fuzzy coercion are stored at 0.75 not 0.95, and an elicitation.put{status} counter for T23. Final: A's precedence, bands and plan, with those B pieces.

final.chosen: Typed codec at the single merge point (put) + source precedence table with CHOSEN equal to ANSWER and a direct-answer override rule + PutOutcome with bounded rivals + one set of confidence bands + a typed ProfileIn and one profile-to-slots mapper used by the browser projection, the server profile row and the entry subtype.
final.why_chosen: put() is already the one door every fact passes, so typing and precedence there fixes profile, extractor, model notes, lever choices and future document writes at once. Reusing answers.validate means a profile value and a spoken answer normalise the same way. Equal-rank CHOSEN/ANSWER with an explicit direct-answer override protects choices from offhand extractions while still letting the founder correct themselves; low-rank disagreement becomes a question, as the flag resolution asks. The bands give the stop rule, selector and restatement one meaning of 'known'.

design.algorithm: put: unknown key -> unknown_slot; coerce fails -> rejected (nothing stored). No existing -> stored. Same normalised value -> stored with max confidence and higher-rank source. New rank > existing rank -> stored, previous becomes rival. Equal rank >= 3 (ANSWER/CHOSEN/PROFILE): later wins only when answering=True (direct answer to that slot's question or explicit correction); otherwise kept_existing + rival. Equal low rank (EXTRACTED/NOTED) with different value -> conflict: keep existing, add rival, cap confidence at TAU_ASK - 0.01 so the slot is asked. New rank < existing rank -> kept_existing; differing value added as rival; no confidence change when existing rank >= 3 so an offhand sentence never reopens a direct answer. A founder ANSWER resolves a conflict and clears rivals.

verdicts.reasoning: Both teams found the same cause (two-valued _apply returning False on None, with the extra IS_FALSE-passes-on-missing bug; untyped founder/startup dicts with diverging key names; status and money meaning missing from Scheme; support_for bypassing the engine) and chose the same fix: Kleene three-valued evaluation, a typed Pydantic FounderFacts, a catalogue join for status/money/equity, seed-catalogue consistency test, and support_for routed through the engine. B is more complete and safer in five places: (1) a TypeError during comparison also yields UNKNOWN with a log, never FALSE; (2) it renames seed rule paths and catalogue inputs to FounderFacts paths with extra='forbid' and a path-resolution test, rather than A's permanent input-alias layer that keeps two spellings alive; (3) status is checked first so closed/revamping/not_in_tn schemes land in a not_open bucket regardless of rule result, and it uses the catalogue's real status vocabulary; (4) shortlisted catalogue ids without encoded rules are returned as 'not yet checked by rules', never as eligible, which closes a hole A leaves in support_for; (5) a monotonicity property test (filling an UNKNOWN never turns FALSE into TRUE) and composition with T19 consent redaction (withheld caste becomes UNKNOWN, not a false no). Putting Tri and FounderFacts in app/core lets T29/T24/T19 reuse them. A contributes two things B lacks: needs_info questions ordered by how many schemes each missing field would decide, exported as unknown_inputs(session) to T05's selector as blocked-consumer value (B only gestures at this in its risks), and the explicit rule that sensitive founder fields (caste, special category, gender, age) are never projected from the conversation, only from the consented Schemes screen. Final: B's design and plan plus those two A pieces.

final.chosen: Kleene three-valued evaluator (shared core/tri.py) + typed FounderFacts contract (core/facts.py) with renamed rule/catalogue paths + catalogue join by id for status, money meaning, equity and the structured criteria of encoded schemes + support_for routed through the same engine + needs_info questions ordered by decision value and exported to T05.
final.why_chosen: It fixes the logic in the one evaluator every path uses (Schemes screen, recommend, annotate, /talk) with no dependency: unknown is no longer false, Soundness holds (eligible only when every leaf is TRUE) and every 'no' is a real violation while every 'maybe' names what to answer next. One typed contract stops spelling and case deciding eligibility and is reused by T29, T24 and T19. Joining fast-changing status and money meaning from the curated catalogue moves toward one scheme source without waiting to structure all 46 entries. Exporting the decision value of each missing field lets T05 ask the question that unlocks the most schemes.

verdicts.reasoning: Both teams read the code the same way (budget is len(turns), 9 required IDEA slots versus Q_MAX 7, dynamic questions asked before required slots via a first-come cap, answers in d['answer'] never read, static consumer-count value, no WHY slot, restate omits skipped slots and planner inputs, CP-SAT adding nothing at default size) and both chose one greedy required-first policy over a unified candidate pool with per-source quotas, binding of dynamic answers, a blocked-results value term from T04, and CP-SAT only when a burden budget binds. A is wiser on the core: (1) it resolves the 9-versus-7 infeasibility by design, splitting required slots into must-ask (cannot be guessed) and assumable (capital_band, funding_route) with a declared assume value that a test pins to the planner's defaults, so the restatement says exactly what will be used; B simply stops at Q_MAX and assumes whichever required slots the value order failed to reach, which can drop a slot that cannot be guessed. (2) For F-A1-019 A fixes the panel question itself (fallback to the seat that scored the weakest criterion, skip questions whose dup_slot is known), so offline founders still hear the panel's real concern; B only drops the duplicate, leaving no panel question until T35 lands. (3) A needs only a questions_asked counter plus asked keys and dynamic metadata, while B adds a full AskRecord ledger, a new policy module and a T34 format upgrade for the same behaviour. (4) A drops dynamic questions whose research/council key changed (T06). B adds useful pieces A lacks: a cap of four assumed items in the spoken restatement (most-blocking first, rest on screen) so voice stays short; the tie-in to T10's correction reader so one confirmation reply can fix several assumptions; gating sensitive slots by T19 consent purpose rather than only a static flag; and Hypothesis properties (greedy head equals CP-SAT head with a slack budget; questions_asked never exceeds Q_MAX). Final: A's policy and plan with those B pieces.

final.chosen: One QuestionPolicy in the selector: budget counted in questions actually asked, must-ask versus assumable required tiers with declared defaults, dynamic (scan/panel) questions as bound, quota-limited candidates, a blocked-results value term from T04, greedy lexicographic selection with CP-SAT only when a burden budget binds, and a restatement that names every assumption and gap (capped for voice).
final.why_chosen: Every question goes through one decider that sees the remaining budget and what is still blocked, so the budget means questions, facts that cannot be guessed come first, the panel is not shut out and nothing is asked twice. Declaring which required slots are assumable, with the exact default, makes the 7-question budget feasible without lengthening the interview and makes the restatement truthful. A sort is the exact form of a lexicographic policy and ~700x cheaper than the solver, which is kept only for a binding voice burden budget. It reuses the existing selector, slot table and session document with no new dependency.

design.components: 1) Session: questions_asked (incremented in step() when it returns an ask for a slot or dynamic not asked before; re-asks and opinion turns do not count) and asked_keys; Q_MAX limits questions_asked. 2) Slot table: Need gains ASSUMABLE (required for the stop rule but closable by its declared default when budget runs out); Slot gains assume, assume_label (capital_band -> under_2L 'under Rs 2 lakh'; funding_route -> self 'your own funds') and restate: bool (True for non-text slots whose consumers include roadmap or scheme). Must-ask: problem, solution, beneficiary, sector, product_form, stage, district. A test asserts planner defaults equal slot.assume. 3) Candidate = SlotCandidate | DynamicCandidate{key, question, source: scan|panel, binds: slot | risk/criterion id | 'notes', dup_slot, research_key/council_key}. Dropped when dup_slot or bound slot is KNOWN or its key changed (T06). Quotas: panel <= 2, scan <= 1 (never from the generic 'Any idea' group), total <= 2; a panel arrival replaces an unasked scan one. Dynamics eligible only when must-ask slots are covered or remaining budget exceeds remaining must-ask count. 4) Value = static (W_REQUIRED, W_CLASSES, W_BURDEN) + W_BLOCKED * blocked(key), blocked = scheme decisions UNKNOWN only because of this slot (T04 unknown_inputs, non-sensitive only) + roadmap gates waiting on it; falls back to len(consumers) until T04 lands. Sensitive slots filtered unless the T19 purpose is granted (and SENSITIVE_DEFERRED). 5) Selection: sort by (class rank must_ask=0, dynamic/assumable=1, enriching=2; -value); CP-SAT only if the channel's burden budget can bind; select_next called once per step and the plan passed to is_objective_clear. 6) Stop: must-ask covered and (assumable covered or questions_asked >= Q_MAX) and fingers satisfied; WHY covered by any of why_now, differentiation, motivation at band ASSUMED or better (extraction included); if none, ask differentiation once only if budget remains, else name WHY as a gap. 7) Dynamic answers: bound to a slot -> put() as Source.ANSWER (T03); bound to a risk/criterion -> session.founder_notes; otherwise founder_notes 'notes'; notes passed to council and planner and restated 'You told me ...'; offline 'Things to think through' list excludes queued/asked points. 8) Panel question (vote.py, rules.py, seats.py): each seat question tagged with dup_slot (customer seat -> beneficiary) and binds; with no criterion spread > DISAGREE, ask from the seat that scored the weakest criterion; skip when dup_slot is KNOWN. 9) restate(): core sentences; 'I assumed: ...' for every restate slot in band ASSUMED or from EXTRACTED/NOTED/DEFAULT (team_size, founder_years, time_horizon, geo_scope included) and for unasked assumable slots with assume_label; 'You skipped X; I will assume Y' for skipped/dropped required slots; gaps include skipped slots. On voice at most 4 assumed items, most-blocking first, the rest on screen; T10's correction reader lets one confirmation reply change several.

verdicts.reasoning: Both teams named the same cause (nothing declares which inputs a derived result depends on: idea_version at ideation.py:136-142 hashes every core slot, levers have no id or patch, jobs are keyed (session, kind) with LATEST although results.py already accepts a version key, narration marks are global and positional) and chose the same build-system style fix: declared input keys per artefact kind, key-tagged jobs/results/narration/artefacts, stable lever ids with patches, late rendering, panel ranking of all levers, and re-confirmation after a post-roadmap lever choice. B is a little stronger on safety and migration: (1) its risk mitigation runs each job's work function on a snapshot built only from inputs(kind, s), so a job physically cannot read an undeclared input; that enforces the completeness of the manifest, which is the single way this design fails, whereas A only compares lists in a test; (2) it maps old 'statement'/'lever:i' marks to the current research key on read so resumed sessions do not repeat narration; (3) it wraps artefacts in a uniform {key, kind, built_at, data} envelope, adds a 'what changed' line between versions, a gate so experience mode without a chosen card creates no key or job, and a property test that keys are stable across processes (no built-in hash()). A is better on lever patches: B's localise and cost-down levers patch nothing, so choosing them changes only chosen_levers; A gives localise a geo_scope patch and routes cost-down and regulatory-route levers into founder_notes, which the council key reads (and which ties in with T05's founder_notes), so those choices visibly change what the panel and roadmap see. B also names a 'LEVER' source; the final uses T03's Source.CHOSEN. Final: B's design and plan, with A's patch table and founder_notes in the council key.

final.chosen: Declared derivation keys per artefact kind (research_key, council_key, plan_key) computed from a dependency manifest, key-tagged artefact envelopes, jobs, results and narration marks, structured levers with stable content ids, slot/notes patches applied as Source.CHOSEN and narration-time rendering, panel ranking of all levers, and re-confirmation when a lever is chosen after the roadmap.
final.why_chosen: Declaring what each result depends on answers 'would this result come out differently?' directly: filling sector no longer re-searches, a lever adding search terms does, a lever changing only the plan re-runs panel and roadmap but not the search, a key always exists once there is text, a late old result is rejected by comparison, and keyed marks make a new verdict audible. It needs only hashlib and the ResultStore interface that already takes a key, works with the in-process board (no Redis), and is reused by T11 and T31. Running jobs on manifest-only snapshots enforces the manifest's completeness.

verdicts.reasoning: Both teams identified the same cause (no store contract for durability, lifetime, read purpose and failure; 'saved' inferred from store.name == 'database' which CachedStore's 'database+redis' breaks; _expired applied at every layer so Redis re-hides what the DB returned; read-fill without a version guard and delete dropping the copy before the row; store kind chosen once per process; cohort reusing the live read per id) and the same solution: durable flag and one Lifetime, TTL-only cache, Lua compare-and-set with a tombstone, retry + breaker with memory for new sessions and 503 for existing durable ones, and a get_many analytics read with a cohort_consent column. B fits the repo better: it reuses the existing services/breaker.py Breaker class (verified at backend/app/services/breaker.py:18) instead of hand-rolling a second breaker; it stores the Redis copy as a hash {v, doc} so the Lua script compares a field without cjson-decoding the whole document; it extends the existing hand-written FakeRedis in tests/unit/test_redis_layer.py rather than adding fakeredis with its Lua extra (a new test dependency), with an optional real-Redis CI job; it makes retention a setting so decision D4 changes one value; and it promotes a memory-born session into the database on its first save after recovery so saved flips to true instead of the conversation being lost on restart. A contributes two details B misses: removing the dead and contradictory ElicitationSession IDLE_EXPIRY (30 days) and expired() (verified at session.py:35 and :142), which otherwise remain a third lifetime clock, and reporting sessions_found / sessions_not_found in the cohort response so a programme officer can see when ids have aged out. Final: B's design and plan with those two A details.

final.chosen: Explicit SessionStore contract (durable, kept_until, live get, analytics get_many, delete) with one Lifetime policy and delegating wrappers, a version-guarded Redis copy (Lua compare-and-set on a {v, doc} hash plus a delete tombstone), and a FallbackStore that reuses services/breaker.py: retry once, 503 for existing durable sessions, memory for new ones, half-open re-probe and promotion of memory-born sessions on recovery.
final.why_chosen: Every flag is a symptom of callers inferring behaviour from store names and layers re-deciding expiry, so the lasting fix is one contract the wrappers delegate to. The cache race is cross-process, so only an atomic server-side guard closes it, and EVAL is free through the installed redis-py. The outage path reuses the Breaker class already in the repo, so the store re-probes instead of deciding once per process, with no new dependency. get_many fixes analytics counts and cost in one query and is the interface 5.5.5 can later replace.

design.components: backend/app/agents/lifetime.py: Lifetime(cache_ttl = settings.session_cache_ttl_hours (6), retention = timedelta(days=settings.session_retention_days) (90, D4)) with kept_until(s, durable) ('until this server restarts' when not durable) and retained(s). ElicitationSession.IDLE_EXPIRY and expired() removed (dead, contradictory). SessionStore protocol: durable: bool; get(id) (live, retention-bounded, no idle hiding); get_many(ids, *, consented_only=True) (analytics: no cache fill); create; save; delete(id) -> bool. MemoryStore durable False; SqlStore durable True; CachedStore delegates durable/kept_until, applies no expiry of its own (Redis TTL only), CAS put, tombstone delete; FallbackStore(primary=CachedStore|SqlStore, secondary=MemoryStore, breaker=services.breaker.Breaker('database', threshold=2, window_s=30, cooldown_s=30)). StoreUnavailable mapped to 503 with Retry-After in core/errors.py. Routers return persistence {saved, kept_until} on start, resume snapshot and every turn/done; Talk.tsx banner from it. routers/cohort.py uses get_many and reports sessions_found and sessions_not_found.
design.data_model: agent_sessions gains cohort_consent BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false (backfilled from the document; written by create/save) and an index on (cohort_consent, last_active). Redis: sess:{id} becomes a HASH {v, doc} with EXPIRE cache_ttl; gone:{id} tombstone with EXPIRE cache_ttl. Settings: session_retention_days = 90, session_cache_ttl_hours = 6. AgentSession gains home: 'database'|'memory' (not persisted).
design.algorithm: CAS put (KEYS sess:id, gone:id; ARGV version, doc, ttl): EXISTS gone -> 0; HGET v >= version -> 0; else HSET v doc, EXPIRE, return 1. get: Redis hit returns doc; miss -> inner.get -> CAS put (stale read cannot overwrite newer; deleted id cannot be refilled). delete: SET gone:id EX ttl -> inner.delete -> DEL sess:id; save conflict still drops the copy. FallbackStore: primary calls retried once after 200 ms on OperationalError/DBAPIError/OSError/TimeoutError, then breaker.fail(); while open, create() goes to memory (durable False), ids held in memory are served there, any other id raises StoreUnavailable ('This conversation can't be reached right now; try again in a minute'); half-open re-probes; a memory-born session is created in the database on its first save after recovery so saved flips true. Auto mode at boot always builds FallbackStore (no sticky choice). get_many: one SELECT ... WHERE session_id = ANY(:ids) AND cohort_consent AND last_active > now() - retention; consent filtered before parsing; MemoryStore filters its dict; CachedStore delegates without filling Redis.
design.rollout: 1) durable + persistence field + Lifetime with TTL-only cache and dead constant removed (fixes resume-then-404 and the banner; no schema change). 2) CAS cache + tombstone (old string keys ignored, expire within 6 h). 3) FallbackStore replaces the once-per-process auto choice. 4) cohort_consent migration (after T16 makes migrations safe) and get_many. Each step covered by the parametrised contract suite.
design.offline: MemoryStore alone implements the same contract (durable False, kept until restart). FallbackStore without a database behaves like today's memory mode but re-probes every 30 s. Without Redis, CachedStore is not built; Redis errors are swallowed as today.
